continuous_drift.scope: independent diagnostic fixture; excluded from walking evaluation
continuous_drift.interpretation: All groups consume identical recorded truth, actions, measurements and prior. Signed one-step bias and multistep MSE describe the mean model; whitened residual moments describe bias/scale/correlation mismatch in process noise; time-binned posterior errors and coverage describe the combined filter. These are localization evidence, not a causal ablation or walking score.

verification.followup_targeted_tests: Report 15, orchestration 12, drift 4 passed after type narrowing; GPU diagnostic regression 19 passed.

pyright.scope: Only PyTorch public symbols flagged as private exports and MuJoCo compiled binding attributes missing in dependency stubs. No repository rule disabled. Report modules independently pass with zero errors.

implementation_incidents: Strict GPU continuation initially differed by floating-point roundoff under first-use TorchScript specialization. The independent verifier now uses force_eager and optimized_execution(False); all three groups passed bitwise without tolerance relaxation. Training protocol unchanged.

GPU actor-gradient diagnostics initially loaded CPU joint-calibration metadata into a CUDA environment. The inference view now transfers only that metadata tensor; real A/B/C diagnostics completed. Existing snapshots and scores preserved.

A rounds 1-5 used the initial profiling field names physical_timeouts and warmup_rounds; the former includes all replay truncations. Later rows use physical_truncations and process-local warmup_rounds_in_process. Post-save memory was added after these five rows; their saved evidence covers pre-save peaks only.
interpretation: Single training seed and two validation episodes per candidate; all walking validation episodes failed. No claim of method effectiveness or C superiority.
Real and imagined learning curves use different start distributions. Independent critic and fixed-record process/posterior scores are reported separately.

On common walking records, nonzero mean bias and large whitened residual second moments coexist with poor posterior coverage. These localize model/calibration concerns without proving a causal filter defect.
The five-second supine record is ground-supported and outside the walking distribution; it is a diagnostic fixture, not walking control performance.
Neither local CPU nor GPU complete online path meets 20 ms in current eager implementation. Robot hardware latency has not been measured.
